title: UGC NET Paper 1 Full-Length Grand Mock Test 2024

questions.question_text: Which of the following levels of teaching involves the highest level of cognitive interaction, where learners actively formulate hypotheses and solve unstructured problems?
questions.explanation: Hunt's Reflective Level represents the highest cognitive stratum in teaching hierarchy. At this level, students engage in deep inquiry, critical evaluation, problem solving, and reflective thinking beyond rote recall (Memory level) and conceptual relationships (Understanding level).
questions.numerical_formula: Cognitive Hierarchy: Memory Level (Herbart) < Understanding Level (Morrison) < Reflective Level (Hunt).
questions.common_pitfalls: Students frequently confuse Morrison's Understanding level with Hunt's Reflective level.

questions.question_text: In experimental research, when an unobserved external variable concurrently influences both the independent variable and the dependent variable, causing a spurious association, it is called a:
questions.explanation: A confounding variable is an outside influence that changes the effect of a dependent and independent variable. This risk is resolved via randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or ANCOVA statistical controls.
questions.numerical_formula: Spurious Correlation: r_xy driven by hidden z => Partial correlation r_{xy.z} = (r_{xy} - r_{xz}r_{yz}) / (sqrt(1-r_{xz}^2)*sqrt(1-r_{yz}^2)).
questions.common_pitfalls: Confusing intervening variables (which mediate the path X -> M -> Y) with confounding variables (which cause both X and Y).

questions.question_text: According to Classical Nyaya Indian Logic, which of the following pramanas refers to knowledge derived through comparison and analogy (e.g., recognizing a wild cow 'Gavaya' based on prior description)?
questions.explanation: Upamana in Nyaya epistemology is defined as knowledge of the relation between a word and the object denoted by it, attained via similarity to a known object (Sadrisya-jnana).
questions.numerical_formula: Pramanas in Nyaya: Pratyaksha (Perception), Anumana (Inference), Upamana (Comparison), Shabda (Verbal Testimony). Note that Arthapatti is accepted by Advaita Vedanta and Mimamsa, NOT Nyaya.
questions.common_pitfalls: Remember that Nyaya accepts only 4 pramanas; selecting Arthapatti for Nyaya questions is a common exam trap.

questions.question_text:
With respect to IPv4 vs IPv6 addressing, which of the following statements are correct?
(i) IPv4 addresses are 32-bit whereas IPv6 addresses are 128-bit.
(ii) IPv6 utilizes IPSec as a mandatory native protocol standard.
(iii) IPv4 uses dot-decimal notation, IPv6 uses colon-hexadecimal notation.
(iv) Broadcast addressing is present in IPv6.
questions.explanation: Statement (iv) is FALSE because IPv6 completely eliminates broadcast addressing in favor of multicast and anycast. Statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are strictly true.
questions.numerical_formula: IPv4 Address Space: 2^32 (~4.3 x 10^9 addresses). IPv6 Address Space: 2^128 (~3.4 x 10^38 addresses).
questions.common_pitfalls: Never select options claiming IPv6 has broadcast; broadcast is exclusively IPv4.

questions.question_text: Under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 2015-2030), which SDG specifically targets 'Quality Education'?
questions.explanation: SDG 4 is 'Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all'. SDG 3 is Good Health & Well-being; SDG 5 is Gender Equality; SDG 8 is Decent Work and Economic Growth.
questions.numerical_formula: SDG Mnemonic: 1-No Poverty, 2-Zero Hunger, 3-Good Health, 4-Quality Education, 5-Gender Equality, 6-Clean Water.
questions.common_pitfalls: Candidates frequently mix up MDGs (8 goals by 2015) and SDGs (17 goals by 2030).
